neighbours.label: predicate of a clause about when one event happens relative to another (don't wait until … to ▸, even though … were ▸ only in, whereas … have ▸); quiet without the timing relation
fire: The choir was finished by 1240, even though the bell tower was begun only in 1310.
Please don't wait until the night before the exam to open your textbook.
The effects of the drought would not be fully felt until the following harvest.
Give the glue a few minutes to set before you move on to the next joint.
Seedlings keep putting on height through August, whereas mature trees have already stopped growing.
The treaty was signed in March, although its terms did not take effect until the autumn.
Make sure all the files are saved before the installer starts copying anything.
The bridge opened to traffic in 1932, even though the approach roads were completed only in 1936.
quiet: The choir of the old abbey is narrow, and the bell tower is built of red brick.
Please bring your textbook and a pencil to the exam room.
The drought damaged the wheat, the barley and most of the vegetable crop.
Use the stronger glue for the joints on the legs of the chair.
Seedlings in the nursery are shorter and greener than the mature trees outside.
The treaty was signed by both ministers in a large hall in Geneva.
The installer copies the files into a folder on the desktop.
The bridge carries four lanes of traffic and has two stone approach roads.

notes: Card + look: top examples are 'even though the cloisters were begun only in', 'don't wait until a storm is coming to purchase', 'not be fully felt until', 'a chance to settle before continuing'; the - pole's output promotes begin/start/happen/completed. Probe: timing-contrast sentences 0.48-0.89, plain sentences 0.01-0.09.
